newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P assigns BBB- to Hyundai unit's secured debt.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns BBB- to Hyundai unit's secured debt.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Tuesday it had assigned its BBB- ratings to Hyundai Semiconductor America Inc's (HSA) planned issue of $200 million of senior secured notes due in 2004 and $200 million of senior secured notes due in 2007.
S&P said the outlook for the rating was stable.
HSA is a wholly owned unit of Hyundai Electronics America Inc, which in turn is 75.7 percent owned by South Korea's Hyundai Electronics Co Ltd and 24.3 percent by other Hyundai Group members.
S&P said that as one of the world's largest semiconductor makers, the credit quality of Hyundai Electronics was adequate.

It said the ratings reflected the key positions of the two U.S. subsidiaries in the global operations of Hyundai Electronics and the financial flexibility it and its subsidiaries derive from being a core businesses of the Hyundai Group, one of Korea's largest and strongest groups of companies.
